title: A recursive notion of form
as_he_states: The opening proposes recursion in dimension and repeatedly revises the data for dimension one. The cancelled axiom list is explicitly provisional.
plausible_today: A category of objects with a specified equivalence notion, together with a theorem for a fixed tame or conically smooth class; not a universal topological reconstruction from bare incidence.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. Malgoire2002 describes the figure-first program; AFR2019 Theorem4.2.5 gives a fully faithful exit construction under its conically smooth stratified-homotopy conventions. Neither supplies the missing induction for these definitions.
why_open: The source proceeds through successive axiom systems; it gives no historical explanation of why the general program was not completed.
worth: Worth a later comparison only after the final atelier vocabulary and its retained data have been fixed.

title: Do support and endpoints determine a segment?
as_he_states: He asks whether injectivity is an extra assumption, then states support injectivity in Corollary4.
plausible_today: F1 and the side-containment/separation clauses of F2 already imply support injectivity and endpoint uniqueness among subsegments of a fixed segment.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. The complete elementary proof is R-SA21-support. Hua2026 Theorem76.1 contains the corresponding local uniqueness step in a single-segment model; no novelty claim is made.
why_open: Resolved within the author’s sequence by an asserted corollary; the written proof is abbreviated, not an abandoned global problem.
worth: Worth incorporating as a short proved lemma in the companion, not a new research task.

title: What strengthening does the branch axiom need?
as_he_states: The margin says to complete F3, and the later local filtering statement depends on it.
plausible_today: Common nontrivial initial subsegments must be downward filtered inside a fixed segment; then the intended germ relation is transitive.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. R-SA21-branches checks this step. Hua2026 Theorem76.1 explicitly includes the reconstructed F3′ but excludes general branch transitivity from its claimed formalized scope.
why_open: The source itself notices the omitted condition. The exact wording of the marginal formula remains a scan question.
worth: Worth settling in a fixed axiom-version table before checking any global orientation theorem.

title: Which tame-arc examples satisfy F5 or F6?
as_he_states: The proposed embedded-arc example is followed by an unfinished qualification about F5 or F6.
plausible_today: Choose an exact PL or semialgebraic category; verify each axiom separately, and impose one-dimensional branch conditions when asking for exactly two germs.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. The open-primary regular-neighborhood literature and Esquisse discuss controlled local geometry, but neither is an exact theorem about this F1–F6 list. Plane arc germs already show that two-branch behavior is additional.
why_open: The qualifying sentence is unfinished; no explanation beyond the working revision is supplied.
worth: Worth a compact example audit once the intended tame category is stated.

title: Which restrictions preserve a network?
as_he_states: After asking the question in a cancelled draft, he asserts inheritance under every subset.
plausible_today: Require at least closure under all ambient F4 composites needed by retained pieces; order-convex subsets work in the checked interval models.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. R-SA21-restriction refutes arbitrary inheritance, including strengthened ambient F1–F5 and both F6 versions. Hua2026 expressly does not prove the restriction claim.
why_open: The source asserts an answer without checking the gap created by nonexhaustive gluing. It does not give a later explanation of this failure.
worth: Worth a bounded theorem on admissible restrictions; the unrestricted question is already answered negatively.

title: Quotients of the singular lieux
as_he_states: He announces an equivalence relation on singular lieux as a future enrichment after cancelling the critical-locus version.
plausible_today: Specify the equivalence relation and require compatibility with supports, endpoint pairs and branch germs before forming a quotient network.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. No exact quotient theorem was located in the recorded native-vocabulary searches; Malgoire2002 confirms only the broader figure-based setting.
why_open: The relevant definition is deferred and no compatibility axioms are supplied in these cotes.
worth: Worth retaining as a definition-design question, with low priority until a realization target is fixed.

title: Coherent global orientation
as_he_states: For a connected regular model, all endpoint and branch pairs should identify coherently into exactly two orientation classes; he says that if false it must become an axiom.
plausible_today: For a specified final axiom list, prove the transport graph is connected and every closed transport has trivial permutation holonomy, or exhibit a model with nontrivial holonomy.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. R-SA21-orientation isolates the exact elementary obstruction. Hua2026 Theorem76.1 handles only one ambient segment and explicitly leaves the global orientation question aside. No exact resolution was located.
why_open: He explicitly says the verification is absent and proposes an additional axiom if the statement fails.
worth: High-value bounded task: normalize transports and test the first possible closed configurations.

title: Local versus global directedness
as_he_states: The attempted proof of global filtering from local filtering and connectedness is withdrawn.
plausible_today: The local assumptions alone do not suffice; add a common-extension condition of the appropriate F6 strength.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. The rational ordinal-sum fork is completely checked in R-SA21-fork. It also explains exactly where F6 fails. No external theorem is needed to negate the original implication.
why_open: The author identifies a counterexample on the pages and introduces F6 immediately afterward.
worth: Useful as a warning lemma in the companion; no further run is needed for the negative answer.

title: Equal-endpoint segments and the circular case
as_he_states: An early cancelled draft predicts a circle-type two-segment exception; later he claims endpoint branch distinction and intersection only at the endpoints, but stops mid-proof.
plausible_today: Separate the endpoint-branch lemma under strong F6 from the weak-F6 version with singular endpoints, then complete the intersection proof before proposing a classification.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. The source-specific search located no exact completion; Hua2026 explicitly excludes these last pages. The earlier run’s weak/strong-F6 counterexample refutes an equivalence, not the equal-endpoint lemma itself.
why_open: The supplied last page ends in an unfinished formula; the early classification belongs to a cancelled version.
worth: High interest, moderate one-run reach: settle the precise two-segment lemma before any global classification.

title: Which endpoints must F6 retain?
as_he_states: The first F6 explicitly omits the other endpoints; a later reformulation includes whole supports, and the equal-endpoint argument refuses to assume the other endpoint regular.
plausible_today: Treat interior extension and support extension as different axioms. The regular-end reduction is conditional on a proved prolongation lemma.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. The two-maxima rational order in R-SA21-weakF6 verifies strict inequivalence at singular ends. Hua2026 excludes F6 and the general F4 prolongation corollaries.
why_open: The source itself states the endpoint limitation; the later alleged equivalence does not resolve its interaction with singular ends.
worth: Worth checking the general prolongation corollary and then the special singular-end use in one focused run.

title: Topological realization of abstract réseaux
as_he_states: The title of coteII announces topological realizations, but the package develops constructions rather than a realization-and-recovery equivalence.
plausible_today: Fix a source category, a target category and whether the comparison is homeomorphism, isotopy, weak equivalence or stratified homotopy. Retain attaching and link data appropriate to that choice.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. McCord1966 Theorems1–3 concern weak homotopy; BarmakMinian2008 Theorem3.10 concerns simple equivalence; Clader2009 Theorem1.1 and corrected Lemma3.1 concern a specific barycentric inverse system and quotient; Stacks09XV obstructs a connected Hausdorff space as a raw finite-space inverse limit. None proves the proposed literal cutting-system equivalence.
why_open: No such theorem is formulated in the supplied early pages; the finite-pro-object suggestion belongs to the earlier planning context.
worth: High conceptual interest but a few-hour run should only specify and test one exact comparison.

title: Regularity after cutting and the cone lemma
as_he_states: He acknowledges that the first cut-piece argument lacks regular immersion, adds Li c, and invokes a two-cone lemma.
plausible_today: Require the two closed pieces to cover a neighborhood in the cone lemma. For contractions, keep the ends disjoint from the contracted set or recheck all quotient end conditions.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. R-SA21-cone-cover supplies the cover repair. R-SA21-side-contraction gives a connected finite tripod counterexample to the literal side-contained contraction claim. The PL regularity subcase is proved by a height-function construction.
why_open: The first missing condition is explicit. The further cover and contraction defects are mathematical diagnostics of the literal transcript, not claims about the ink.
worth: Worth a short corrected local-cutting theorem in a fixed PL category.

title: What is the category in the cutting equivalence?
as_he_states: The pages announce equivalences between cut ficelles and lists of pieces with specified gluing homeomorphisms, without giving morphisms.
plausible_today: For compact Hausdorff admissible pieces, choose endpoint-preserving homeomorphisms compatible with every gluing map and prove cutting/pushout are quasi-inverse; treat isotopy quotients separately.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. Esquisse §5 describes boundary-attaching pushouts and their noncanonical choices. The closed-pushout reassociation and n+1/n count are checked here, but no published exact equivalence in this ficelle language was located.
why_open: The manuscript labels the construction for memory and passes to the order on lieux rather than writing a full categorical proof.
worth: High one-run reach for a precise elementary theorem once morphisms and admissibility are fixed.

title: Connected ends, existence and interval classification
as_he_states: He claims existence precisely for connected nontrivial compact triangulable spaces, proposes connected or contractible ends, and gives an interval classification.
plausible_today: For reduced structures on connected finite polyhedra, existence and unique-pair iff arc are true. The unrestricted necessity and interval classification require correction; endpoint connectedness repairs the latter.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. R-SA21-disconnected and R-SA21-interval refute the two broader assertions. R-SA21-polyhedra proves the reduced statements. The native ficelle formulation was not located in the searched literature; standard noncut-point theory is comparison background, not a substituted theorem.
why_open: The source itself notices a connectivity issue when retracting endpoint enlargement but does not explicitly retract all neighboring assertions.
worth: Worth publishing precise companion lemmas and counterexamples; no broad new classification is warranted.

title: Equivalence classes of oriented ficelle structures
as_he_states: He conjectures that all oriented structures on a triangulable X are equivalent under endpoint inclusions, then rejects this already for a segment.
plausible_today: Classify only after fixing the permitted end category and the exact inclusion-generated equivalence. The connected-end interval subfamily has two orientations.

why_open: He explicitly writes that the conjecture is false already in the segment case.
worth: Moderate interest; a few-hour run can classify the interval or a small graph under a chosen end restriction.

title: Property-P restrictions on cuts and links
as_he_states: He suggests imposing P on ends, internal loci and both relevant conic links to preserve the cutting-order properties.
plausible_today: Give sufficient closure conditions on P and the allowed embeddings; distinguish point, ball, sphere and bicollared examples rather than one unrestricted assertion for every intrinsic P.
state_of_art: As of 19 November 2026. Esquisse §5 discusses tame gluing and stronger isotopy comparisons; AFR2019 Theorem4.2.5 requires conically smooth stratified data. These are partial frameworks, not a proof for arbitrary P.
why_open: The source offers examples and a recommended hypothesis, without a uniform theorem or proof.
worth: High interest, low general one-run reach; begin with one concrete PL property and an explicit interpolation construction.

title: The rive comparison and the implicit relative spectrum
as_he_states: The page identifies the rive algebra with clopens of a conic link, asserts a section formula under paracompactness, and writes an implicit Spec producing a boundary over A.
plausible_today: Use closed A in paracompact Hausdorff X and the relative Stone space of (i_*F₂)|A. Keep this distinct from the global ring spectrum and the étalé space of elements.

Gillam2011 supplies relative ringed-space localization; Hua2026 Theorem77.1 verifies the explicit rive-to-boundary injection. The cylinder calculation separates the three possible spaces.
why_open: The spectrum base/topology is left implicit; the ordinary sheaf theorem itself is not an unresolved new problem.
worth: Worth a precise convention and comparison lemma before constructing full cuts.

title: Regularity of the full spectral cut
as_he_states: He asserts regular-immersion transfer to the full boundary and its clopen parts; a doubtful reciprocal margin may ask for a converse.
plausible_today: First define the full cut as a topological space over X and prove the relevant quotient and properness facts; then formulate forward transfer and any converse separately.

title: When does the partial cut characterize a maille?
as_he_states: A maille with one node and a birive should be equivalent to the corresponding partial cut being a ficelle.

worth: Worth a dedicated compact-conic test after the full-cut definition is settled.

title: May the nodes always be reduced to points?
as_he_states: A marginal note suggests reducing A1,A2 to points, with uncertain wording and scope.

title: Symmetry of two-node maille compatibility
as_he_states: The final page asserts that the condition relating two disjoint nodes and their two birives is symmetric.
plausible_today: In a fixed cut model, formulate the four retained side germs and show successive cuts commute under precisely stated connectivity and regularity conditions.

as_he_states: The abstract definition postpones disjoint lieux; coteII develops a stronger-than-set-disjointness geometric compatibility and an order.

The later pair-cut/betweenness theorem in Hua2026 §78 concerns its own ordered setting, not an automatic topological realization of every early réseau.

title: Recovering a finite cut from its compatible complement
as_he_states: For finite compatible subsets T of a set L equipped with a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, put C(T)={x outside T: x compatible with every t in T}. The marginal assertion is that C(T) determines T, and C(T)⊆C(T′) implies T′⊆T. The offered argument assumes compatibility of a selected t∈T′ with T, which the bare data do not ensure.
plausible_today: Additional axioms must make the complement operation injective; bare reflexive symmetric compatibility does not.
state_of_art: The three-vertex counterexample is checked in this run. No exact external fate found in S03,S06; it does not refute any later strengthened network axioms.
why_open: The page writes Oui and starts a proof; its selected point need not be compatible with the other cut. No historical explanation for the gap located.

as_he_states: Boundary and finite-cut equivalence data should follow from the two-point cutting data in the proposed network axioms.

title: Intrinsic axioms for betweenness and pair-cut networks
as_he_states: Find conditions on R(a,b,c), or on S0 and the RE, that are equivalent to a biordered tronçon structure.
plausible_today: An exact characterization must include global bidirectedness, density and stability under nonempty strict cones, and must specify strict versus non-strict betweenness.

title: T0 and sobriety of the canonical tronçon topology
as_he_states: Is every abstract tronçon T0, or sober, in its canonical topology?

title: Does closedness of points force a total order?
as_he_states: For totally ordered L points are closed; is the converse true?
plausible_today: No: R² with equality-or-strict-coordinate order has Euclidean strict-interval topology and is not totally ordered.

why_open: The parenthesized converse at III23 has no answer on the pages.

title: Closing strict intervals in the augmented topology
as_he_states: After adding complements of closed intervals/rays, do closures of strict intervals/rays equal the corresponding closed pieces, with the stated endpoint exclusions?

as_he_states: Is {X,Y} moderated iff X∧Y exists?

as_he_states: An induced refinement should be the infimum for refinement; its emptiness should detect disjointness.

as_he_states: Find the least target stratum of a refining elementary figure, then prove admissibility of all closed shadows.

as_he_states: Separate conditions for existence of induced refinements from conditions making them commute with induction; find minimal axioms.

title: Places, elementary figures and subdivision-minimality
as_he_states: Characterize places as minimal figures; the converse should hold for ball-like objects.
plausible_today: Refinement-minimal nonempty figures are elementary and subfigure-minimal. No proper subdivision is a weaker condition; the claimed ball case needs a geometric model.

as_he_states: Determine equivalences among residual partition, intersection and saturation conditions; the first finite independence example is rejected.

as_he_states: Complete the remaining directions of the compatibility proposition; determine stability of allowed geometric subfamilies under joins.
plausible_today: The four compatibility criteria hold for admissible families; local-finiteness restrictions are generally stable under finite, not arbitrary, joins.
state_of_art: Direct proof in the manuscript checked here; modern Alexandrov representation is background (WWY-1). No exact external multistratum formulation located.

title: Recovering subfigure inclusion from refinement and subdivision
as_he_states: Can ≤ be expressed using ≪ and ≼ alone?
plausible_today: The stated necessary condition (a subfigure that subdivides is equal) does not supply a definition of ≤. A reconstruction theorem or two nonisomorphic subfigure orders with the same remaining data is needed.

worth: High interest: finite admissible-family systems give concrete data for a reconstruction or counterexample search.

title: Restriction and extension axioms C6/C7 in the set model
as_he_states: Verify uniqueness of induced subfigures and extension of a prescribed subdivision.
plausible_today: Both hold for admissible subset families; extension is realized by the least finer topology on a fixed closed support.

title: Characterizing the least extension by its outside strata
as_he_states: Conditions b,c,d should be equivalent and should characterize the least extension.
plausible_today: The common-closed-stratum lemma and d⇒b,c are false; b⇔c survives. The four weak topological tests are insufficient. Preserving closures of every subset outside the closed locus is the correct condition.

title: Universal property of lower-ideal replacement
as_he_states: State the poset replacement separately and use its terminal property to infer leastness.
plausible_today: The replacement is terminal among diagrams preserving the specified lower part and complement identification; this does not force arbitrary bijective outside maps to be isomorphisms.
state_of_art: Direct order proof checked; standard Alexandrov functoriality is background. No exact external historical match for this presentation located.

worth: Moderate interest: write the correct diagram category and universal property explicitly.

title: Least finer topology extending a closed-subspace topology
as_he_states: Construct the least finer topology, describe closed sets and closures, and establish the converse characterization.
plausible_today: For closed T⊂S and σ finer than τ|T, closed sets are A∪B with A τ-closed, B σ-closed in T; closure is clτ(X∩U)∪clσ(X∩T).

title: Homotopical properties of the replacement map
as_he_states: Quotient, connected-fiber, contractible-fiber and homotopically proper universal weak-equivalence properties should pass from the replaced locus to the whole map.
plausible_today: Quotientness, point-fiber assertions and principal-lower-ideal contractibility pass as stated. The universal claim needs a precise definition of properness and allowed base changes.

worth: Yes: fix the intended homotopical-properness definition before testing universal base change.

title: Which relations determine an atelier?
as_he_states: Check the refinement-supremum/zero-infimum characterization of disjointness (VI13 “Vérifier”); determine whether refinement alone or face inclusion plus subdivision determines the remaining structure.

as_he_states: Does the large multiombre give the announced equivalence with families of set figures, with no forgotten At* axiom, including finite-type versions?
plausible_today: Use complete join-prime elementary figures, the least-receiving-face property, immediate-refinement transitivity, exact family closure conditions, and hereditary finite generation if every subfigure is required to have finite type. title: Small-shadow faithfulness, morphisms and inverse-image constructions
as_he_states: When do small shadows recover an atelier, and which operations on figure sets produce covariant or contravariant stratum maps? Does every map of sets induce the proposed figure pullback?
plausible_today: Complete local downset homomorphisms are inverse images of unique monotone maps without sobriety. Global faithfulness requires separate injection/refinement/compatibility hypotheses. The naive closed-preimage construction must remove empty open strata or restrict the allowed maps.

title: Additional linking data for pseudodisk reconstruction
as_he_states: Recover geometry from shadow data enriched by the missing links between pseudodisks.
plausible_today: First specify the geometric category, the incidence/link object, equivalence notion and reconstruction functor; no strongest precise theorem can be extracted without those choices.
state_of_art: Esquisse §5 pp25–27 discusses canonical decomposition of stratified spaces and gluing pieces, with isotopy addressing noncanonical choices. It does not define this pseudodisk invariant. S67-03,05,06,11 found no exact later theorem; CSG still lists VGF as unpublished.

title: Subatelier closure, density and saturation
as_he_states: Does a lower family inherit all axioms, is the large-shadow image spacious, and can an atelier be saturated through thick/quasi-dense subateliers?
plausible_today: Require Sousat2 in addition to lowerness, and disjointness reflection for inheritance of L2. Any saturation must state which compatible/infinite unions it adds and verify that it preserves the intended refinement and loci.
state_of_art: The saved three-point example refutes unrestricted At3 inheritance. Downset closure methods are standard (Speed1968), but no exact thick/quasi-dense saturation theorem for this two-order structure was identified in S67-02–05,11,12. Malgoire2002 supplies only historical presentation evidence.
why_open: The manuscript corrects the lower-family claim and explicitly postpones saturation; the L3 inheritance argument has an unresolved direction reading.
worth: Worth a finite countermodel audit first, because a saturation that changes disjointness would change virtual supports.

title: Compatibility and disjointness axioms in set-like examples
as_he_states: Which locus tests recover compatibility, and is disjointness stable under refinement without further assumptions?
plausible_today: State stability as D0 or derive it from a fully specified L2/locality system. Distinguish pure set intersection, geometric compatibility and strict/polyhedral refinement; retain the empty-or-elementary common-face condition only in the polyhedral variant.
state_of_art: Exact atelier-axiom searches S67-02,03,05,11,12 found no published resolution. Opened polarity literature explains how an orthogonality graph yields supports, but does not justify geometric compatibility from arbitrary set shadows.
why_open: A selective-compatibility obstruction leads the author to add disjointness axioms; the later strict-refinement repair changes the intended examples.
worth: Worth checking on explicit small models before extending the axiom ladder.

title: Finite versus arbitrary gluing of refinements
as_he_states: Check restriction, compatible gluing and the implication diagrams; isolate the existence axiom needed for infinite families.
plausible_today: Use the least-receiving-stratum inverse-image construction for restriction, At11′ for finite compatibility and a distinct directed local-supremum existence axiom for infinite gluing. The choice of intersection class Σ must be fixed.
state_of_art: SGA4 ExposéII Definition2.1 gives the sheaf matching-family paradigm; it is a formal comparison because its objects/sites are not these ateliers. No exact At11/At11bis theorem was found in S67-05,08,11. Massas2023 handles only the local lattice maps.
why_open: VI79–81 explicitly retracts a diagram that conflated finite compatibility with infinite join existence.
worth: Worth proving the finite and directed parts separately; the first concrete step is an axiom-by-axiom restriction/gluing proof.

title: Support witnesses and subdivision maximality
as_he_states: Can an external witness separating the orthogonality profiles of F′≪F be found inside F, and does equality of profiles characterize face-maximal refinements?
plausible_today: Retain the support-witness axiom, L2 and restriction locality; use maximality in face order, not refinement order. Any stronger common-refiner requirement is a different set-like hypothesis.
state_of_art: Lindenhovius–Vetterlein2023 §§1,3 verifies the polarity background and shows why support equality is weaker than Boolean/set behavior. Searches S67-01,07,09–12 found no exact atelier maximality theorem. The P4 model checks the old witness axiom but not optional absorption.
why_open: The manuscript alternates axiom/proposition labels and reduces to an elementary/locus case; it does not remove the reduced hypothesis.
worth: Worth a focused independent proof because this is the bridge from geometric subdivision to virtual support.

title: Finite type makes the directed local-existence axiom vacuous
as_he_states: Check the brief assertion that a locally finite increasing refinement family is stationary when all figures are of finite type.
plausible_today: With face-directed increase, local face suprema, finite generation of each figure and complete join-prime elementary objects, the family is eventually constant. Do not replace these by refinement-directed increase.
state_of_art: Independently proved in formalism_and_checks.md §3 from the standard compactness of finite joins of complete join-primes. Speed1968 verifies the pre1986 representation mechanism; no external exact atelier wording was found.
why_open: The manuscript only gives a parenthetical assertion. The analyst’s initial concern was resolved after checking the strong definition of irreducibility.
worth: No new research is needed for this precise version; retain the proof and test only genuinely different variants.

title: Polyhedral duality and the weak simplex criterion
as_he_states: Check self-duality under interval inductivity and the claimed finite-poset characterization of a simplex; use strict refinement for geometric examples.
plausible_today: Keep chain-completeness hypotheses in the order-duality lemma. Replace the false predecessor-count criterion by Boolean principal intervals; a square is a complete counterexample to the written criterion.
state_of_art: Stanley1991 §1 p319 states the Boolean interval definition of simplicial posets and the meet-semilattice specialization to simplicial complexes. It does not validate the manuscript’s weaker test. The square certificate checks every written hypothesis.
why_open: The simplex induction misses that not every subset of minimal elements must occur as a face. No later self-correction occurs in the supplied VII pages.
worth: Worth a short editorial correction and a scan check; the false criterion itself is settled by the saved example.

title: Atfil for refinement-increasing families
as_he_states: May face-increasing be replaced by refinement-increasing, and should the supremum then be taken for refinement?
plausible_today: Treat this as a separate theorem with an explicit order of directedness, restriction notion and local-stationarity hypothesis; the face-order theorem does not answer it.
state_of_art: SGA4II Definition2.1 supplies only a gluing analogy. S67-05,08,11 found no exact two-order directed-union result for these axioms.
why_open: The margin leaves the choice open and the following corollary gives no full proof.
worth: Worth a small-model dependency search before attempting a general proof.

title: Strong support witnesses and common refiners
as_he_states: If Y is disjoint from G but not from F, with G≪F, can one choose a nonzero witness refining both Y and F?
plausible_today: The claim needs a common-refiner/disjointness equivalence such as AtensD; it is not expected in arbitrary orthogonality spaces. For loci it becomes x not⊥F⇒x≪F, a strong set-like condition.
state_of_art: The opened orthogonality-space paper Lindenhovius–Vetterlein2023 distinguishes generic polarities from stronger geometric axioms; it contains no general common-refiner theorem. Exact searches S67-07,09–12 found none.
why_open: The manuscript itself says this is scarcely true except for set-like ateliers and isolates it as an extra axiom.
worth: Worth identifying the exact additional condition, not pursuing it as an unconditional conjecture.

title: Completeness and redundancy of the ML reconstruction
as_he_states: Recover the atelier from M, two orders and the locus graph, proving the ML lemmas and the final theorem without missing hypotheses.
plausible_today: Use the strengthened ML1 lifting condition, nonempty interior loci, receiving-face coverage and the graph disjointness axiom. Restore the common-ambient hypothesis in Lemma1 and VII41 LemmaA before applying their conclusions.
state_of_art: Speed1968 and Massas2023 establish the one-order/downset component. No exact ML0–5 two-order reconstruction was found in the recorded named-database and terminology searches S67-02–05,11,12. Malgoire2002 only confirms later exposition.
why_open: The proof itself forces ML1 to be strengthened on VII28; later formulations replace the same machinery with Prat and Mag.
worth: Worth a rigorous proof consolidation because the strongest statement is already identifiable and several omitted hypotheses are localized.

title: Which infinite figure families are determined by elementary data?
as_he_states: When does a preatelier determine its figures uniquely, and what must be added for infinite or locally finite figures?
plausible_today: Finite deployments are forced precisely with finite principal ideals and lower compatible finite unions. Infinite figures require an explicit admitted lower family and join closure. Finite generation alone requires hereditary finite generation and is a distinct condition.
state_of_art: The downset construction is standard (Speed1968; Massas2023), but no exact classification of the manuscript’s admissibility choices was found in S67-02–05,11,12.
why_open: VII61 explicitly notes the extra choice for general figures, while VII114 omits lowerness in its finite formula.
worth: Worth stating as an elementary classification with counterexamples separating finite deployment and finite type.

title: Dense test objects Λ and the failure of graph-only reconstruction
as_he_states: Can lieux be replaced by any dense Λ and compatibility reconstructed solely from disjointness on Λ?
plausible_today: A dense testing family must also detect disjointness and satisfy the common-refiner lifting/locality axioms. Density alone is insufficient; keep the compatibility relation primitive until those implications are proved.
state_of_art: No exact MΛ/PratΛ result was found in S67-02,03,11,12. Generic orthogonality closure in Lindenhovius–Vetterlein2023 does not supply a face/refinement relation or the missing lifting axiom.
why_open: The author explicitly writes “Non” and cancels the attempted derivation at VII48–50.
worth: Worth preserving as a documented failed simplification, then testing the minimal repaired list.

as_he_states: Do the set-like locus axioms imply a faithful embedding in Fig(L), and are Pratquas1–4 sufficient?
plausible_today: Separate local subfigure-lattice isomorphism, global injection, compatibility reflection and refinement reflection. The latter need additional hypotheses; strict/polyhedral refinement can remain stronger even with injection.
state_of_art: Massas2023 Theorem2.30 answers the local lattice question only. The manuscript’s affine/PL and strict-refinement examples show the global converse fails. S67-02–05,11,12 found no exact later global reconstruction under just the written axioms.
why_open: The author retracts successive converse proofs on VII58–59 and leaves the quasi-set adequacy claim tentative.
worth: Worth fixing the exact morphism/embedding definition before using this theory categorically.

title: Canonical supports for interval figures on a poset
as_he_states: Construct a canonical point/cell realization for intervals over an arbitrary poset, including intervals with empty interior.
plausible_today: Start with a totally ordered interval model or explicitly impose intersection/face conditions on the poset. Formal cells can retain endpoint versus open-interval information, but a full functorial realization needs stated axioms.
state_of_art: The opened VGF catalogue and Malgoire2002 give no exact interval realization theorem. S67-03,05,11,12 found no later publication matching the arbitrary-poset formulation. Standard Boolean/polarity representation does not preserve its incidence and refinement data automatically.
why_open: VII70 makes a broad claim without checking all poset intersections, and VII72 asks for a canonical construction; the earlier III tronçon construction has narrower hypotheses.
worth: Worth a tightly bounded finite-poset audit followed by a total-order theorem.

title: Do the strengthened faithful-surjectivity conditions force an isomorphism?
as_he_states: Under pairwise orthogonality faithfulness of α and the condition cF(ᾱα*(y))=cF{y}, where α*(y)={x:α(x)⊆cF{y}}, must α_*:ΣE→ΣF be bijective? The preceding inclusion-only argument is distinct and is corrected on scan67.
plausible_today: Yes: the closed values cFα(x) preserve and reflect orthogonality and are join-dense in ΣF; Proposition2 then gives a unique ortholattice isomorphism. The inclusion-only version is false (P1).
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-031/032, independent P1/P5. Classical Galois-completion ingredients: Birkhoff1948 IV §§6–7. A modern join-dense subset presentation appears in PasekaVetterlein2025 Proposition2.4, with a unique-zero convention requiring adjustment for the manuscript.
why_open: The manuscript says the assumptions may be too strong and later proves the more general representation criterion; no external source was found explaining any historical abandonment.
worth: No new research is needed for the stated implication; it is worth making the internal resolution explicit in the companion commentary.

title: Complete the enveloping-support representation and its dense-subspace formulations
occurrences: scan82 J156-9-11:6–17 (formulation b′ and explicit-formula reminders)
as_he_states: Represent a spatios by a faithful disjoncteur of generators; give the inverse formulas and the alternative injectivity condition b′; identify which subdisjoncteurs are dense enough to give the same spatios.
plausible_today: A faithful orthogonality map with join-dense image yields ΣE≅L. For D⊆E, ambient support join density is equivalent to restriction injectivity and to the closure map ΣD→ΣE being an isomorphism. The point-preorder density phrase requires an explicit convention; its purely intrinsic supremum interpretation is false in the empty-D one-point example.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-032/045–051; independent P5–P6. Birkhoff1948 IV §7 and PasekaVetterlein2025 Lemma2.3/Proposition2.4 provide checked completion and modern presentation results. The uncertain injection word and missing D quantifiers are in readings.tsv.

worth: An exact comparison of redundant-point presentations is a useful bounded exposition task after the scan readings are checked.

title: Discharge Proposition3’s deferred closure identities without circularity
as_he_states: The support-level adjunction is stated with inserted identities b); their proof is deferred, and the first attempted argument is crossed out before a replacement based on the raw pretranspose identity.
plausible_today: A raw point pretranspose gives the subset adjunction; orthogonality is unchanged by source closure, which yields both closure identities. Conversely support adjunction plus those identities recovers raw point adjunction. The support adjunction by itself is insufficient.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-052 and P4; countermodelP3. CoeckeMoore2000 §3 supplies the support-level orthogonal adjoint; PasekaVetterlein2025 Lemma3.5 checks the closure consequence in its point-map setting.
why_open: The cancelled argument attempted to use the support formula before establishing compatibility; the live replacement completes the deferred step on scan93.
worth: The proof is complete; the cancelled circular route should remain documented but is not a research problem.

title: Does the generator extension and categorical composition really work?
as_he_states: The arbitrary-function lemma and the later corollary require checking that the extension preserves joins and recovers its generator values. The text also leaves a reminder to check composition before announcing the normalized category.
plausible_today: Arbitrary assignments fail; compatible closed-valued assignments are exactly fσE for a join map f. Composition is closure after setwise composition, identity is σE, and the support functor is fully faithful and essentially surjective. The transpose reverses composition.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-035/054–056, P2/P4/P7. Exact later correspondences: DomenachLeclerc2001 Theorems4.1/5.1; canonical-category conjugation: CoeckeMoore2000 §3[3.4]. The pre-1986 Galois foundation is Shmuely1974.
why_open: The author supplies the missing pointwise equality and completes the corollary on scan99. The final categorical assertion is justified by those corrected bijections; it does not validate the earlier unrestricted lemma.
worth: This is settled; checking exact source dependence and map normalization is valuable editorial work rather than a new theorem search.

title: Does OR-product closure coincide with closed-fiber correspondence closure?
as_he_states: Can correspondences be interpreted as supports of E×F with disjunction given by an OR in the two coordinates? Closed supports have closed rows and columns; the converse is doubted except when one factor is trivial.
plausible_today: The converse is false in general and true when one factor is a trivial disjoncteur. Four-point paired-orthogonality factors yield a three-point diagonal with closed fibers and full product closure. The product formula itself needs its cross-factor indices checked on the scan.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-057/058; proofP8 and exhaustive16-point certificate. Exact tensor comparison: Ischi2010 Theorems3.4 and3.6, primary preprint pp.6–7. Published issue2010, online2011, arXiv2011 as separately recorded.
why_open: The supplied pages record doubt but give no reason for subsequent abandonment; the later tensor results are mathematical matches, not evidence of direct historical transmission.
worth: The universal question is answered; identifying restricted geometric factor classes where the two closures agree could be useful, but is a separate research task.

title: Can all correspondences between two spatios form a spatios?
as_he_states: Hom∨(L,M) is complete under pointwise order; does it admit a complement C or disjunction relation making it a spatios? The trivial-source case is a product M^E.
plausible_today: No in general: for the six-element four-atom ortholattice L, Hom∨(L,L) has234 maps,40 atoms and16 coatoms, so it admits no order reversing bijection. The trivial-source product case remains true; complement is pointwise on generator values only.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-059–062, independent P9/P11 and executed certificate. Ischi2010 Theorems3.6/4.9 give a matching negative result through minimal versus maximal weak tensor products. Shmuely1974 §6 gives completeness of the Galois-map lattice.
why_open: The manuscript recognizes that the complement is unclear. The structural obstruction is that complete map lattices need not be self-dual; no source was found documenting the author’s historical reason for leaving this question.
worth: No further work is needed on the universal assertion; a sharply specified restricted correspondence class might support a different positive question.

title: Which point substitutes could support a correspondence geometry?
as_he_states: The possibility of a complement on correspondences seems tied to identifying minimal nonzero elements or other objects playing the role of points.
plausible_today: The universal hoped-for consequence cannot hold even for finite atomistic ortholattices, by MP-SA21-109. A viable statement must first specify the admissible objects, map class and desired point representation; the manuscript does not choose these here.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-063. Ischi2010 gives a direct obstruction; CoeckeMoore2000 and PasekaVetterlein2025 develop particular adjoint categories, with extra hypotheses in their point-space representations. The bounded search found no exact continuation of this unformulated programme.
why_open: No source provides a historical explanation. The text expresses a heuristic link rather than a precise conjecture, so it cannot be declared solved by topical similarity.
worth: Low priority until the intended geometric examples and allowable morphisms are fixed, because atomisticity alone already fails.

title: Can every correspondence factor through a span of morphisms?
occurrences: continuation scan105 J156-9-14:6 (these questions are set aside); scan107 same:83 (no general decomposition available)
as_he_states: The graph of an ordinary relation yields an inverse-image map followed by a direct-image map. Does every general correspondence similarly factor as a comorphism followed by a morphism, where a comorphism commutes with C and a morphism has transpose commuting with C?
plausible_today: No for these definitions: the map f on the six-element four-atom L with f(0)=f(a)=0 and f(b)=f(c)=f(d)=f(1)=a cannot equal h†g for any complete ortholattice K and C-preserving join maps g:L→K,h:L→K. For nontrivial K, h reflects zero and forces f(1)=1; trivial K forces f=0. A factorization under weaker maps is a different question.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-064–066, P10–P11; executed join-preservation check plus symbolic proof for all intermediateK. The recorded searches found no exact external result for this span. CoeckeMoore2000 §3 verifies the transpose formalism used in the proof, not the factorization.
why_open: Scan105 says these questions do not immediately bear on the set formalism of ateliers; scan107 explicitly proceeds without such a decomposition. This explains the local change of focus, not any undocumented later decision.
worth: The literal universal problem is settled negatively; a worthwhile new task would first identify map classes appropriate to the geometric examples rather than ask the same false universal question.

title: Which powerset-map identities survive for general spatios?
as_he_states: For conjugate join maps of spatios, determine when orthogonality preservation implies meet/difference preservation and, with top preservation, complement preservation; he hopes suitable commensurable or constructible supports suffice.
plausible_today: The unrestricted implication is false even for a complete lattice embedding B4→O6 preserving orthogonality and top. A useful correct formulation must require Boolean compatibility of the images of the relevant complementary partitions, or specify an equivalent exact hypothesis.
state_of_art: As of2026-11-19: C-SA21-9-086 and certificate general_spatios_corollary_failure give an independent negative answer in the unrestricted case. Janowitz1963 pp1241–1242 treats orthogonal adjoints in orthomodular lattices; Paseka–Vetterlein2025§§3–4 treats adjointable orthoset maps with explicit hypotheses. Neither is an exact theorem for the manuscript’s unspecified constructible restriction. Searches S9E-01–05 plus shared S67 relation/support families found no exact matching formulation.
why_open: On scan107 he says his proofs use severe hypotheses close to Booleanity and worries that global supports create irrelevant problems; no external historical reason for abandonment was found.
worth: Worth a narrowly defined follow-up: characterize the image-partition condition for complement preservation before attaching geometric terminology.

title: Both conjugate maps preserve complement: are they inverse?
as_he_states: If α_* and its orthogonal transpose β_* both commute with complement, are they inverse spatios isomorphisms?
plausible_today: Yes, for complete ortholattices and exact conjugacy u(a)⊥b iff a⊥v(b); no Boolean or orthomodular hypothesis is needed.
state_of_art: Independent proof C-SA21-9-088/R-SA21-9E-002: complement converts the conjugacy into both u⊣v and v⊣u. Ore1944 gives the older Galois framework; Janowitz1963 p1242 records orthogonal adjoints, while Paseka–Vetterlein2025 uses the same exact conjugacy. The manuscript itself inserts “oui”.
why_open: The page answers the question affirmatively in the margin but leaves the proof unwritten.
worth: No separate research project is needed; include the two-adjunction proof in the folder commentary.

title: Do the Boolean-pair conditions always hold, or force global Booleanity?
as_he_states: Are the comparable-pair/orthogonal-family conditions automatic for spatios, at least finite ones, and if imposed do they force Σ Boolean, perhaps after strengthening to infinite orthogonal families?
plausible_today: They characterize orthomodularity, not Booleanity. O6 disproves automatic validity; MO2 is complete, nonBoolean and satisfies the arbitrary-orthogonal-family condition. The10-element manuscript example needs the listed ink checks before literal acceptance.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-090–095,098; Janowitz1963 p1241 and Lemma1 identify the standard orthomodular/commutation condition. Harding–Navara2011 discusses MO2 and Boolean subalgebras. Finite certificates check all hypotheses and the infinite-family reduction for MO2. The original Dacey1968 thesis was sought but not obtained; LV2023 Lemma3.4 supplies the modern exact criterion.
why_open: The author recognizes the issue locally and supplies a later diagram; the pages do not connect his condition to the established name orthomodularity.
worth: Worth resolving in the commentary through a terminology concordance and the two smallest countermodels, with no claim of a new open problem.

title: Orthomodularity of strict-comparability polarities of posets
as_he_states: Determine what happens when the disjoncteur relation on an ordered set is x<y or y<x.
plausible_today: Not always orthomodular: the height-two poset0<1,2<1,2<3 has comparability graphP4 and support latticeO6. A classification would require further order-theoretic hypotheses.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-094/R-SA21-9E-004. LV2023 Example3.3 and Jenča2024preprint/2026publication Example2.6 give the exact P4 obstruction; its orientation as the manuscript’s strict-comparability relation is verified here. An11Aug2026 correction exists; its metadata were opened, but the corrected theorem was not accessible and is not asserted.

title: Can commensurable refinement form an atelier?
as_he_states: Can one restrict spatial figures to commensurable supports and strengthen refinement by joint commensurability, while preserving transitivity? Are residue-family tests sufficient for entire diagrams?
plausible_today: For arbitrary complete ortholattices the strengthened refinement of commensurable discrete figures is nontransitive. The residual criterion is valid after explicitly requiring each predecessor-fiber plus residue to reconstruct its parent; this is available underγ². Orthomodular ambient lattices avoid these particular nonBoolean-block defects.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-100–105; R-SA21-9E-007,008. The18-element certificate verifies the complete ortholattice and the two adjacent Boolean8 subalgebras, while endpoint generation yields nonBoolean18. Janowitz1963 Lemma1 explains why orthomodularity improves compatibility. No exact later publication of this atelier construction was identified in S9E-01–07 and shared support searches.
why_open: On scan123 he explicitly identifies the possible nontransitivity and says the proposed construction does not seem to work; he also questions whether it is expressible on strata alone.
worth: Worth a follow-up on corrected categorical objects or additional hypotheses, starting from the saved18-element obstruction.

title: Does faithful external support imply joint commensurability?
as_he_states: Does a faithful external support in VIIIp62 implyγ³, especially for faithful morphisms? He compares a Corollaire1 at an uncertain page71/74.
plausible_today: No for faithfulness as explicitly defined in VIII68–71: a normalized faithful external realization of the discrete P4 atelier fails even supp1. Full faithfulness is a different, stronger condition and must be investigated separately.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-106/R-SA21-9E-005 and its complete certificate give the negative answer. Both source endpoints were read: VIII68 conditions(i)–(iv), VIII71 Suppfid, and VIII87 Corollary1, which actually uses full faithfulness. LV2023 Example3.3 supplies the established P4 lattice; the external realization is our independently checked construction. No exact published atelier theorem was found by the bounded searches.

worth: Worth including the counterexample immediately; a new research run should address the fully faithful version rather than repeat the false weaker implication.

title: Intrinsic constructible supports and localization by subdivisions
as_he_states: Construct the supports relevant to a figure independently of the global spatios, with complement and partially defined commensurable joins/meets; possibly recover closed constructible supports by inverting subdivisions in(F,≪). Is the resulting category thin and does it embed inΣ?
plausible_today: Specify the partial algebra and the actual classW first. A calculus of fractions/common-refinement theorem can make localization manageable, but a separate theorem must prove thinness and identify the support image. None follows merely becauseF is a poset.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-107,108. Stacks§4.27 Definition4.27.1 and Lemma4.27.2 give exact sufficient conditions for the fraction construction and cite Gabriel–Zisman1967I§2. SGA4II§§1–2 and Esquisse§5 are useful conceptual comparisons, not this construction. Named-database and exact-term searches found no matching atelier theorem. The original Gabriel–Zisman book was not inspected.
why_open: Scans124–127 explicitly object to composing unrelated supports and state uncertainty about both thinness and the embedding; scan128 lists other tasks to pursue first.
worth: High-interest follow-up once the subdivision axiom is fixed: check the Ore square condition on small explicit ateliers and state the intended universal property.

title: Support embeddings for four subatelier constructions
as_he_states: For open-shadow, figure/maquette, strict residual and compatible broad-residual subateliers, verifyΣ_A′↪Σ_A.
plausible_today: Each case needs a specified map and specified preserved operations. Candidate maps by ambient closure are generally different from literal inclusion of subsets; an orthogonal adjunction or a separation criterion may provide an embedding.

The exact four constructions have no matched published embedding theorem in S9E-01,03–05/sharedS67 atelier searches.

worth: Worth one bounded run that checks the four cases separately and records which lattice operations each candidate embedding preserves.

title: From provisional atelier morphisms to virtual-support maps
as_he_states: Choose a morphism notion covering subateliers, inverse images and injective direct images, then determine whether it always induces a conjugate correspondence on associated spatios and whether its kernel is a support.
plausible_today: The bare three-relation pointed maps form a category and have open-refinement-lower kernels, but automatic support-closedness fails. A closure-compatible or adjointable morphism condition must be added; the elementary-generator map must also be distinguished from full figure pullback.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-116–121/R-SA21-9E-009,010. The P4endpoint-deletion certificate verifies a nonclosed kernel under exact IX134zero conventions. Paseka–Vetterlein2025 Lemma3.8 proves closed kernels under adjointability, a stronger hypothesis; IX90–97 itself already requires closure compatibility for lifted correspondences. No exact published atelier equivalence was found.
why_open: Definition134 is explicitly provisional, omits earlier VIII condition(d), and scan135 already anticipates supplementary conditions; scan137 defers the support analysis.
worth: High-interest follow-up: compare the provisional category with the closure-compatible morphisms already developed earlier in IX.

title: Universal excision by an open-refinement-lower subset
as_he_states: ForN lower under≪°, constructA/N universal among maps killingN, and decide whether its kernel is exactlyN. Treat the set-figure example and maquettes.
plausible_today: The maquette constructionA\N is valid for everyN with the provisional zero conventions. The general existence and exact-kernel properties require proof in the actual atelier axiom class; the set example must separate closed-support killing from open-top-stratum killing.

Exact searches for Grothendieck atelier/excision yielded no published general solution. Stacks localization is an adjacent universal construction, not an answer to this quotient problem.

worth: Worth a follow-up beginning with finite set figures and exact kernels; the maquette base case is already resolved.

title: A direct image of figures for a noninjective set map
as_he_states: He doubts that there is a direct figure map for noninjectiveg:E→E′ and asks for a support-level test of the injective direct-image case.
plausible_today: The naive images of open strata can overlap and fail to form a figure. A canonical corrected pushforward would need a specified coarsening rule or universal property. At support level, a disjointness-preserving relation map is direct image by an injection exactly when its transpose preserves complement.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-118,119 and exhaustive set_relation_classification settle the support criterion. Ore1944/Massas2023 establish the relation/powerset context; they do not construct a corrected figure pushforward. The exact atelier/figure searches found no such publication.
why_open: The source gives only the obstruction expectation and an uncertain marginal criterion, not a functorial definition.
worth: Worth only after deciding which face/incidence data a pushforward must retain; the support criterion needs no further research.

title: Final subdivision axioms and local support detection
as_he_states: Compare fiberwise coverage, total support equality, absence of disjoint refining strata/loci, and face-inclusion maximality; a quotient-topology strengthening is considered and canceled.
plausible_today: Fiberwise versus total equality is valid with joint Boolean commensurability. Recovering fiber coverage from absence of disjoint local refinements additionally needs a local density/detection property unless the named Atmag supp² already contains it. The canceled quotient-topology equivalence must distinguish generated comparabilities from single-pair lifting.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-125–128/R-SA21-9E-011,012. The Boolean3-stratum certificate shows commensurability alone cannot prove(iii)⇒(ii); its applicability to the named source axiom is explicitly conditional. A separate finite-poset certificate checks the deleted quotient-topology claim only at the poset level. No exact published theorem identifying these final atelier axioms was found in the bounded searches.
why_open: The page self-corrects maximality from≪to⊂ and cancels the extra topology requirement. The discrepancy in the support-axiom label cannot be resolved without the scan.
worth: High-priority follow-up: identify the exact supp² ink and test the local detection implication before using the final subdivision equivalences.

title: Moderation and saturation after the set-theoretic framework
as_he_states: The next tasks are subdivisions, moderate ateliers and saturation axioms/constructions for an atelier or atelier-magasin; morphisms and their support relation may come first.
plausible_today: A research task must select one stable axiom version and a defined saturation operation. No universal saturation or moderation theorem with all hypotheses is yet stated in this list.
state_of_art: The list is a source program rather than a precise theorem. CSG’s checked unpublished-work catalogue and Malgoire’s2002 seminar notice document continued interest, not a published solution. Esquisse§5 gives the broader stratified-topology motivation; exact atlas/atelier searches found no identified theorem matching this unfinished list.

worth: Worth preserving as program context, but cut any follow-up into a concrete axiom-completion question rather than a general saturation project.
